contraindications: Phenytoin and fosphenytoin: documented Stevens-Johnson syndrome to phenytoin; do not re-expose.
interactions: Valproate + lamotrigine: valproate inhibits lamotrigine glucuronidation, roughly doubling lamotrigine levels; higher risk of serious rash, including SJS, and of lamotrigine toxicity.
Lacosamide + lamotrigine: additive sodium-channel effects; dizziness, diplopia and ataxia; lacosamide also prolongs the PR interval, so obtain a baseline ECG.
Levetiracetam + lamotrigine or escitalopram: no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interaction; additive somnolence with an extra levetiracetam dose.
Lorazepam or midazolam + escitalopram: no relevant pharmacokinetic interaction; additive sedation.
Escitalopram + other QT-prolonging drugs: additive QT prolongation.
output.proposed: A repeat benzodiazepine and a second-line antiseizure medication (levetiracetam, lacosamide or valproate) with maintenance lamotrigine, levetiracetam and escitalopram
warnings: Carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine: cross-reactive severe cutaneous reactions are reported after phenytoin SJS; use with caution.
Valproate: major teratogen; avoid in women of childbearing potential when an alternative exists.

results.finding: An adequately dosed benzodiazepine is the first-line treatment of convulsive status epilepticus, with IM midazolam an effective option without IV access.
Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate were equally effective second-line agents for benzodiazepine-refractory convulsive status epilepticus; lacosamide was not studied.
Seizures continuing after a benzodiazepine and a second-line agent are refractory and are treated with an anaesthetic infusion under continuous EEG.

output.summary: Convulsive status epilepticus is treated at 5 minutes with an adequately dosed benzodiazepine [Glauser_2016]. Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate were equally effective second-line agents in ESETT [ESETT_2019]. Seizures continuing after both tiers are refractory and are treated with an anaesthetic infusion under continuous EEG [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Lamotrigine 8.2 and levetiracetam 42 mcg/mL within range (adherent); bicarbonate 19 after the convulsion; WBC 14.6 and glucose 164; electrolytes, magnesium, renal and liver tests normal; beta-hCG negative
action_criteria.label: Emergency laboratory work-up: glucose, CBC, electrolytes, magnesium, renal and hepatic function, ASM levels, beta-hCG
action_criteria.rationale: Glucose, electrolyte, renal and hepatic derangements are reversible causes of seizures and decide the ASM and its dose; lamotrigine and levetiracetam levels test adherence, and a pregnancy test in a woman of reproductive age changes ASM choice [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Subtle chronic right mesial temporal hypodensity; no acute hemorrhage, mass or edema
action_criteria.label: Non-contrast head CT after stabilization
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes hemorrhage, mass or edema that would change management, and must precede any LP [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Recurrent right temporal-onset electrographic seizures (4-6 Hz, evolving, spreading to the left hemisphere) time-locked to subtle left face and arm clonic activity, with right temporal LRDA between seizures
action_criteria.label: Continuous video-EEG to confirm ongoing seizures and monitor treatment
action_criteria.rationale: Impaired consciousness with only subtle motor activity after midazolam needs EEG confirmation of ongoing seizures; continuous monitoring for at least 24 hours [Brophy_2012]; terminology [ACNS_2021].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Unchanged right hippocampal sclerosis with superimposed peri-ictal diffusion change; no new lesion
action_criteria.label: MRI brain with epilepsy protocol to compare with the prior study and exclude a new lesion
action_criteria.rationale: SE in a patient whose epilepsy had been stable needs MRI to exclude a new structural cause; the prior epilepsy-protocol MRI is the comparison [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum neural antibody panel negative (NMDAR, LGI1, CASPR2, AMPAR, GABA-B, GAD65)
action_criteria.label: Serum autoimmune epilepsy antibody panel (drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy)
action_criteria.rationale: Autoimmune causes (for example GAD65 or LGI1 antibodies) are considered in drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy in adults; a serum panel screens for them [Graus_2016].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Phenytoin and fosphenytoin excluded by the SJS history; valproate would raise lamotrigine levels and is teratogenic; levetiracetam has no relevant interaction; lacosamide needs PR monitoring
action_criteria.label: Drug-interaction check for the second-line ASM (phenytoin SJS, lamotrigine, escitalopram)
action_criteria.rationale: Her documented phenytoin SJS, maintenance lamotrigine and reproductive age decide the second-line drug among options of equal efficacy [ESETT_2019].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on second-line agents after a failed benzodiazepine
action_criteria.label: Literature: second-line treatment of convulsive SE
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give phenytoin or fosphenytoin: documented Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Do not rapidly load or escalate lamotrigine: rash and SJS risk rises with fast titration, and her level is already therapeutic.
Do not start antibiotics or perform an LP for the temperature of 38.1 C alone: it followed the convulsion, without a source, with normal procalcitonin.
required_recommendations: Seizures continue after midazolam 10 mg IM: give one further benzodiazepine dose (IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg, maximum 4 mg) and load the second-line ASM without delay [Glauser_2016].

Load a second-line ASM: IV levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (maximum 4500 mg), or IV lacosamide 200 to 400 mg as an alternative not tested in ESETT; avoid fosphenytoin and phenytoin because of her documented Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and valproate because she is of reproductive age and it doubles lamotrigine levels [ESETT_2019].
Continue video-EEG for at least 24 hours after clinical and electrographic seizure control [Brophy_2012].
If seizures continue after the second-line drug, treat as refractory SE with intubation and a midazolam or propofol infusion under continuous EEG [Brophy_2012].
Continue maintenance lamotrigine and levetiracetam at the current doses, since both levels are therapeutic.
Once stable, refer to a comprehensive epilepsy centre for pre-surgical evaluation: two tolerated ASMs have failed and MRI shows right hippocampal sclerosis.

avoided_actions.rationale: No clinical suspicion of cardiac source of embolus or cardiogenic seizure; routine echo is not indicated in SE workup absent cardiac findings.
No suspicion of arrhythmogenic syncope or cardiac comorbidity precipitating SE; routine telemetry beyond standard ICU monitoring adds cost without yield.
Amyloid PET has no role in acute SE evaluation; dementia biomarker imaging does not change acute management.
Carotid duplex is for ischemic stroke workup; SE without focal vascular suspicion does not warrant carotid imaging.
Polysomnography studies sleep disorders and has no role in the acute evaluation of status epilepticus.

accepted: Focal status epilepticus with secondary generalization in drug-resistant right temporal lobe epilepsy (hippocampal sclerosis)

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Reyes is a 28-year-old Hispanic woman with drug-resistant right temporal focal epilepsy on dual AED therapy who is brought by ambulance after her roommate witnessed a focal seizure with secondary generalization that did not stop. The seizure began with right hand automatisms and dystonic posturing of the left hand, followed by forced head turning to the left, consistent with her known right temporal onset. After approximately 2 minutes the seizure secondarily generalized to bilateral tonic-clonic activity. The roommate called 911 when the seizure had not stopped after 5 minutes. By EMS arrival 8 minutes later, the seizure was still ongoing - now 13 minutes total. She was given midazolam 10 mg IM en route. On arrival to the ED she is still having subtle motor activity with impaired consciousness - 17 minutes total seizure duration. She has a documented phenytoin allergy (Stevens-Johnson syndrome). She was adherent to her medications - both lamotrigine and levetiracetam. She had been under significant stress from her graduate thesis defense scheduled for tomorrow. Sleep deprivation is a trigger for her seizures. She also takes escitalopram.
